deep.reconstruction:
This folio is the printed title page of Christian Leiste, 'Die Arithmetik und Algebra zum Gebrauch bey dem Unterrichte' (Wolfenbüttel, 1790). Leiste was Gauss's teacher at the Collegium Carolinum / Wolfenbüttel milieu, and this was a textbook in Gauss's possession. The printed text contains no mathematics by Gauss. The handwritten '– 1 –' at the right is a foliation or ordering mark.

The only handwritten mathematics visible is on the left edge. It belongs to the facing leaf (the previous page) and is cut off by the binding. The fragments '1/4 x.x-1' (with a vinculum over x.x-1) and '1/4 x' are the tail of the last formula on the previous page. That formula expresses ordinary integrals of falling factorials (x)_n = x(x-1)...(x-n+1) again in the falling-factorial basis:

(a) ∫ x dx = (1/2)(x)_2 + (1/2)x.
(b) ∫ x(x-1) dx = (1/3)(x)_3 + (1/2)(x)_2 - (1/6)x.
(c) ∫ x(x-1)(x-2) dx = (1/4)(x)_4 + (1/2)(x)_3 - (1/4)(x)_2 + (1/4)x.

The margin shows the last two terms of (c): -(1/4)x(x-1) + (1/4)x. The minus sign is lost or illegible at the cut edge.

Verification of (c), my own step. (x)_4/4 = x^4/4 - (3/2)x^3 + (11/4)x^2 - (3/2)x. Adding (x)_3/2 = x^3/2 - (3/2)x^2 + x, then -(x^2 - x)/4, then x/4 gives x^4/4 - x^3 + x^2. This equals ∫ (x^3 - 3x^2 + 2x) dx with zero constant.

The purpose is presumably to have rules for integrating polynomials written in factorial form, as in interpolation and summation of series (cf. the series sums on the previous page). The other faint marks in the margin (stray letters such as 'dt', '=1+t' fragments) are illegible remnants of the facing page's notes on ∫e^{-tt}dt and the substitution t ↦ 2t/(1+tt).
errors: No errors in the visible fragments; the full identities (a)-(c) on the facing page check out exactly. The sign of the term (1/4)x(x-1) must be negative; it is cut off in the margin.

results.what: Integrals of falling factorials expanded in the falling-factorial basis: ∫(x)_n dx = Σ c_{n,k}(x)_k (cases n=1,2,3)
results.modern_name: Conversion between power and factorial bases (Stirling numbers); integrals of falling factorials related to Cauchy/Bernoulli numbers of the second kind

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed title page. The only manuscript content is a cut-off fragment of an elementary, correct polynomial identity from the facing page.

checkable.asserts: ∫x(x-1)(x-2)dx in factorial basis; the margin fragments are its last two terms

transcription_corrections: The marginal fragments '1/4 x.x-1' and '1/4 x' are on the facing leaf (previous page), not this folio. They are the end of the formula for ∫x(x-1)(x-2)dx, and the first should read '−1/4 x(x−1)' (sign cut off).
'– 1 –' at right is handwritten, not part of the printed title page.
Further illegible marginal remnants (e.g. 'dt', '=1+t…') belong to the facing page's notes on ∫e^{-tt}dt and are not transcribed.
